name: Khazar Khaganate
summary: A Turkic trading empire between the Caspian and Black Seas. It stopped Arab advances into the Caucasus, and its ruling elite famously converted to Judaism.

location.value: The Volga–Don steppes, eastern Crimea and the North Caucasus.

terrain.value: Steppe and the lower Volga delta on the Caspian Sea.
terrain.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

climate.value: Dry steppe with cold winters; the Volga delta was wetter and fertile.
climate.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

resources.value: Pasture, fish from the Volga and Caspian, and the tolls of passing trade.
resources.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

disasters.value: No specific disasters are recorded, though floods and harsh winters were likely.
disasters.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

population.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

urbanisation.value: Capitals at Balanjar, Samandar and Atil on the Volga delta.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Khazars (checked 6 Nov 2026); Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

disease.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

migration.value: Multi-ethnic: Turkic, Alan, Slavic, Jewish and Muslim merchants.
migration.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

economicBase.value: One of the foremost trading empires of the early medieval world.

tradeRoutes.value: A crossroad between China, West Asia and Kievan Rus’.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.
wealth.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

moneyAndTax.value: Tolls of about a tenth on goods passing through, and tribute from subject peoples.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Khazars (checked 6 Nov 2026); Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

inequality.value: A ruling Turkic elite above many tributary peoples.
inequality.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

governmentType.value: A khaganate, with a sacred khagan and a military ruler (the bek).

keyRulers.value: Bulan (8th century, linked to the conversion), Obadiah, Joseph (10th century).

succession.value: Within the ruling Ashina-linked family; the khagan was sacred while the bek ran the state.
succession.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

institutions.value: Separate judges for Jews, Christians, Muslims and pagans.
institutions.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

stability.value: Stable for about three centuries, controlling the trade routes between the Caspian and Black Seas.
stability.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

eliteConflict.value: Little is known about internal conflicts in the ruling elite.
eliteConflict.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

armyAndTech.value: Steppe cavalry, and a standing guard of Muslim mercenaries (the Arsiyya).
armyAndTech.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

majorWars.value: The Arab–Khazar wars in the Caucasus (7th–8th centuries).
majorWars.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

territoryChange.value: Estimates vary: about 3 million km² (850) or 1 million km² (900).

alliancesRivals.value: Ally of Byzantium; rival of the Arab caliphate and later the Rus’.
alliancesRivals.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

inventions.value: Little is known; the Khazars were skilled traders and metalworkers.
inventions.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

scienceEducation.value: Little is known, though some Hebrew texts survive.
scienceEducation.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

openness.value: A confederation of many peoples and faiths, with separate judges for each community.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Khazars (checked 6 Nov 2026); Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

communicationTransport.value: Rivers such as the Volga and Don; caravans between the Caspian and the Black Sea.

religion.value: Tengrism; the ruling elite converted to Judaism in the 8th century.

languageWriting.value: Oghuric and Old Turkic; no records survive in the Khazar language.

artsArchitecture.value: The brick fortress of Sarkel on the Don, built with Byzantine help.
artsArchitecture.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

socialStructure.value: The sacred khagan, the bek (military ruler), nobles and tributary tribes.
socialStructure.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

sharedIdentity.value: Unknown; it ruled many peoples of different faiths.
sharedIdentity.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

dailyLife.value: Felt tents in summer and wooden or clay houses in winter in Itil; fish, rice, millet and meat.

neighbours.value: Byzantium, the Caliphate, Volga Bulgaria, Kievan Rus’.

ideasReligions.value: Judaism was adopted by the ruling elite; Christianity and Islam also had followers.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Khazars (checked 6 Nov 2026); Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

colonisation.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

riseSignals.value: Emerged after the Western Turkic Khaganate weakened.

peakPeriod.value: The 8th–9th centuries, controlling the western Silk Road.
peakPeriod.source: Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

declineSignals.value: Attacks by Sviatoslav I of Kiev in the 960s.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Khazars (checked 6 Nov 2026); Golden, Ben-Shammai & Róna-Tas (eds), The World of the Khazars (2007)

outcome.value: Sviatoslav sacked Atil (c. 965–969); successors included Kievan Rus’ and Volga Bulgaria.

sources.value: Arabic, Byzantine and Hebrew sources. Checked against Wikipedia (“Khazars”).

overallCertainty.value: Low to medium. The extent of the conversion is debated. Second source: Wikidata ends it in 1048; Wikipedia’s infobox gives c. 969.

knownFor.label: Jewish ruling elite
knownFor.note: A rare case of a steppe empire whose rulers adopted Judaism.

knownFor.label: Sarkel fortress
knownFor.note: A brick fortress built with Byzantine help.
